title: Scheduled queue freeze exposed priority skew and tail latency regressions
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: During a capacity transition on 2025-02-08 we observed sustained tail-latency regressions for small chat requests and a loss of fairness across priority tiers. The immediate symptom was a multi-minute period where batch formation effectively stopped accepting lower-priority work while high-priority lanes monopolized slots after a scheduled coordinator compaction ran. This ticket captures the RCA, mitigations applied, and action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2025-02-08 02:12 UTC - Autoscaler started a capacity shuffle to rebalance pods in us-west-2
2025-02-08 02:15 UTC - First alert: 95th/99th percentile latency increase on continuous-batcher metric (cb.batch_latency_p99)
2025-02-08 02:16 UTC - Oncall routed traffic to fallback model-variant on dedicated nodes to protect customer SLAs
2025-02-08 02:20 UTC - Investigated batch coordinator logs; noticed compaction job cycle at 02:14 that paused acceptance windows for ~95s
2025-02-08 02:30 UTC - Deployed emergency fix to skip compaction during high ingress (hotfix runtime-1.20.5), latencies returned to baseline
2025-02-08 03:00 UTC - Post-incident stabilization: rollback of compaction heuristic and enabling temporary fairness gate
impact: Affected ~12% of production requests for 18 minutes across two availability zones. Customer-facing error rates were low due to graceful fallback routing, but median token latency increased by ~40ms and p99 by ~320ms for small requests, causing perceptible slowdown for chat UIs and batch-sensitive pipelines.
root_cause: A scheduled compaction/slot-merge routine in the batch coordinator used a global lock and briefly suspended the request acceptance window. During that suspension high-priority 'system' tokens queued up immediately after the window reopened, occupying aggregated batch slots because the scheduler's fairness counters were reset incorrectly during compaction. The combination of acceptance pause and counters reset created a window where lower-priority lanes experienced sustained starvation until KV cache warming and subsequent token arrival rebalanced queues.
contributing_factors: Compaction job held a global mutex for longer than anticipated under rebalanced shard topology
Fairness counters were zeroed instead of preserved during coordinator state migration
Autoscaler activity caused short-lived pod churn increasing compaction frequency
Insufficient observability around acceptance-window state transitions and per-tier queue depth
mitigations_applied: Hotfix: skip compaction when ingress rate > 500 rps per shard (runtime-1.20.5)
Emergency fairness gate: enforce per-tier minimum token allocation for 2 minutes post-compaction
Activated fallback routing earlier in console thresholds to protect SLAs for critical customers
Added temporary alert cb.compaction_hold_time > 50s to paging channel
action_items: ENG-50012 - Replace global mutex in compaction with shard-local compaction (owner: Owen Patel, estimate 5) - due 2025-03-15
ENG-50013 - Fix fairness counter preservation in coordinator migration path and add unit tests (owner: Priya Singh, estimate 3) - due 2025-03-08
ENG-50014 - Add acceptance-window state metrics (state, pause_reason, duration) and dashboard (owner: SRE team, estimate 2) - due 2025-03-01
ENG-50015 - Add canary that injects compaction during low-traffic window and verifies fairness across tiers (owner: Maya Chen, estimate 3) - due 2025-03-10
ENG-50016 - Expand chaos test matrix to include autoscaler churn + compaction overlap in CI (owner: Chaos Eng, estimate 5) - due 2025-04-01
test_plan: Unit tests for counter preservation, integration test that simulates compaction + high-priority traffic, and an e2e chaos scenario in staging that combines autoscaler-induced pod churn with compaction. Each test must assert p50/p95/p99 latency and per-tier fairness thresholds.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge compaction refactor to canary ring (10% traffic) with acceptance-window metrics enabled. 2) Monitor p99 and fairness metrics for 48 hours. 3) Gradual rollout to 50% then 100% with revert playbook. 4) Holdback plan: if cb.batch_fairness_ratio < 0.9 or p99 increases > 15% over baseline, rollback immediately.
comments: 2025-02-10 Maya Chen: Initial RCA drafted. Compaction holds and counter reset look like the minimal repro path. Planning mitigations with Owen and Priya.
2025-02-12 Owen Patel: Implemented temporary fairness gate. Verified p99 returned to baseline in canary. Preparing compaction refactor design.
2025-02-18 Priya Singh: Found edge-case during migration where counters were reinitialized when shard_ids changed. Patch underway with unit tests.
2025-02-24 SRE Lead (Jordan Lee): Added acceptance-window metric to staging dashboards. Recommend running chaos test next week.
2025-02-28 Product (Ava Morales): Confirmed no major customer escalations; UX team requested timeline for fix to communicate to affected partners.
retrospective_notes: We underinvested in observable state for the batch acceptance window and relied on a compaction heuristic that assumed very low pod churn. Moving forward we will: 1) avoid global locks that pause acceptance, 2) ensure state migrations preserve fairness counters, and 3) make compaction safe to run concurrently with autoscaler activity through shard-localization.
next_steps_summary: Execute the compaction refactor (ENG-50012), land fairness counter fixes (ENG-50013), expand tests and dashboards, and run a staged rollout to runtime-1.21. Communicate timeline to stakeholders and update runbooks with the new rollback thresholds.
